feedback: Iteration 3 (entityR2B, 97.74) settles the question I could not answer before. I softened the controller (kp 3.5, base_speed 1.0) on the iteration-2 geometry, and line loss got worse: 0.6 per run on oval and 0.65 on slalom, against 0.25 and 0.3 in iteration 2 and 0 and 0.1 in iteration 1 (entityR2B, 111.80, y 0.03). Softening the controller did not help, so the sensor y 0.02 change and the lower inertia from iteration 2 are the likely cause, as your rationale suggested. Iteration 1 is the strongest evidence: sensors at y 0.03 gave zero line loss on oval and 0.1 on slalom with mass 0.8 and body_length 0.18. Your proposed revert (y 0.03, mass 0.7, body_length 0.14) keeps the inertia gain that helped s-bend progress (0.39 in iteration 2 against 0.14 in iteration 1), so I support it. The current candidate has not raced, so I state no outcome for it. Next steps depend on the race. If line loss on oval and slalom falls to 0.1 or below and max_error stays near 0.063 m, the limit is turn authority, so try wheel_track 0.10 next. If line loss stays at 0.2 or higher even at y 0.03, the mass and body_length reduction is the cause, so return to mass 0.8 and body_length 0.18 (the iteration-1 values) and keep y 0.03.
requested_changes: Keep sensor y at 0.03 with mass 0.7, body_length 0.14, the ±0.06 m span and 16 mm footprints, as proposed. Iteration 3 ruled out the controller as the line-loss cause.
If line_loss_events on oval or slalom is 0.2 or higher after this race, revert mass to 0.8 and body_length to 0.18, the iteration-1 values, keeping sensor y at 0.03.
If line loss returns near 0 but max_error stays at about 0.063 m, try wheel_track 0.10 to raise turn rate per unit of wheel differential. Do not add sensors: line loss is controllable at this span.
